body:
## Proposed changes

Adds a faster non-tick-based socket write locking, which is disabled by default behind a server flag until it can be proven stable; no issues with assertions enabled on demo were found.

This should remove the 25ms delay observed by the player's ping, but might also increase the possibility of work not being shared adequately across players evenly, as the sleep unmounts the virtual thread.

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation Update (if none of the other choices apply)

Closes #13

body:
This pull request introduces significant refactoring and simplification of the `api` package, focusing on modularity, maintainability, and modernized authentication middleware. The changes include removing unused or redundant code, consolidating configurations, and replacing legacy implementations with streamlined alternatives.

### API Package Refactoring:

* [`api/__init__.py`](diffhunk://#diff-d8438cdb658524a2b6e086de042e2cd85ef375b8584204e05e09fd7a0128ce62L2-L36): Removed imports and `__all__` declarations for unused modules and components, simplifying the API package structure.
* [`api/config.py`](diffhunk://#diff-0e3026d2737181f937735ba5e2023ce7f39a7762c8c2594670f4a944a7e48eafL3-R86): Replaced the extensive `dataclass`-based configuration with a simpler, constructor-based `APIConfig` class. Removed unused enums and rate-limiting configurations, consolidating the configuration logic.

### Middleware Updates:

* [`api/middleware/__init__.py`](diffhunk://#diff-dc0c74156988e1d87e04601e402486f5013fe9bfb136001d8736013b80ef69b3L2-L24): Removed imports and `__all__` declarations for middleware components, transitioning to a package-level structure.
* [`api/middleware/auth.py`](diffhunk://#diff-825632565fab79f4178c79bf1e0ff26bb7a2e5d3548a52396b036fb467a71c6aR3-R225): Reimplemented the `AuthMiddleware` to use `BaseHTTPMiddleware` and introduced support for API key authentication. Deprecated JWT-based authentication in favor of a more modular API key service.

### Miscellaneous:

* [`api/data/.gitkeep`](diffhunk://#diff-4d237c903ab813689eba7819b0c2d1736cf9d6d06f2c61f324745e4150742ee0R1): Added a `.gitkeep` file to preserve the `data` directory structure in version control.

# Feature
As requested in #1683, #3819, additional categorization options for accounts would be useful to help manage budget files with multiple related accounts.

# Tasks
Some of the code changes that I foresee modifying include the following:
- [ ] Rework rendering of accounts in sidebar
- [ ] Define a programmatic way to route to top-level account group pages (like the views for "All accounts", "On/Off budget")

## Main Approach
As mentioned in a reply in [#1683](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/1683#issuecomment-2833509524), I plan to define account groups using `/`-delimited account names.

## Potential Blocks
To achieve the tasks above, some considerations should be addressed:
- [ ] How should account reordering work with grouped accounts?
- [ ] Can accounts like "Bank A/Account 1" and "Bank A/Account 1/Sub-account i" coexist?

### Changes

#### 🚀 New Features

-   New hash commands with expiration options support are added - HGETDEL, HGETEX, HSETEX ([#​3570](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3570))
-   Adds option not to raise an exception when leaving context manager after lock expiration ([#​3531](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3531))
-   Add force_master_ip support to async Sentinel client ([#​3524](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3524))

#### 🧪 Experimental Features

-   Adding VectorSet commands support. ([#​3584](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3584))

#### 🔥 Breaking changes

-   Changing the default value for ssl_check_hostname to True, to ensure security validations are not skipped by default ([#​3626](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3626))
-   Updated default value of 'require_full_coverage' argument to true for sync Cluster client to match sync/async cluster APIs ([#​3434](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3434))
-   Adding default retry configuration changes for cluster clients ([#​3622](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3622))
    **Important**:  When instantiating a cluster client `retry` object becomes mandatory.
    -   If retry object is not provided a default one is created with ExponentialWithJitterBackoff strategy and number of retries synced with 'cluster_error_retry_attempts'
    -   **In case a retry object is provided, its number of retries will be used for cluster operations number of retries and 'cluster_error_retry_attempts' will be ignored**
    -   Argument 'cluster_error_retry_attempts' is now deprecated
    -   **For Async Cluster Client the argument 'connection_error_retry_attempts' is completely removed**
-   Updating default retry strategy for standalone clients. **3 retries with ExponentialWithJitterBackoff become the default config.** ([#​3614](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3614))
-   Removing 'charset' and 'errors' inputs from the Redis initialization arguments - deprecated 3 years ago. ([#​3608](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3608))
-   Removing support for RedisGears module. ([#​3553](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3553)). For more info you can check the [deprecated Redis features](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/stack-with-enterprise/deprecated-features/)
-   Removing support for RedisGraph module. ([#​3548](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3548)). For more info you can check the [deprecated Redis features](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/stack-with-enterprise/deprecated-features/)
-   Fixing typing for FCALL commands to match PEP 484 ([#​3537](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3537))
-   Moved ClusterParser exceptions to BaseParser class ([#​3475](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3475))
-   Changed default dialect to 2 ([#​3467](https://redirect.github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/3467)) - This release introduces a client-side default dialect for Redis’ search and query capabilities. By default, the client now overrides the server-side dialect with version 2, automatically appending DIALECT 2to commands like FT.AGGREGATE and FT.SEARCH.
    **Important**: Be aware that the query dialect may impact the results returned. If needed, you can revert to a different dialect version by configuring the client accordingly. You can find further details in the [query dialect documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/interact/search-and-query/advanced-concepts/dialects/).

#### ⚠️ Deprecations

author: mpaiao
body:
This addresses some of the points in discussion #7297 and #5954, and adds a few options for setting up the soil layers and depth to bedrock in ELM without further hard coding. These changes were implemented with the intention of being bit-for-bit with previously generated surface files.

1. The code no longer expects `nlevsoi` in the surface file to be 10 (the default in ELM). Instead, it will use `nlevsoi` provided  in the surface file, as long as `nlevsoi ≤ nlevgrnd`.
2. If `ZSOI(nlevsoi)` is provided in the surface file, ELM will use these layers instead of the default, and append layers between `nlevsoi+1` and `nlevgrnd` if needed using the default parameters, plus an offset to ensure that `zsoi` always increases.
3. The scaling parameters for the soil layers are now declared in `elm_varpar.F90`, to avoid magic numbers.
4. Slightly revised the code that reads the grid-cell dependent depth to bedrock, so it works with either `aveDTB` (the original name in ELM) and `zbedrock` (the name in CLM), so surface files borrowed from CLM would still work with ELM and generate the same soil layers.
5. Deleted some unused variables and (I think) unecessary calls to `check_dim` for `nlevsoi` so the surface file can have different values.


This PR was built on top of #6918 as I was testing ELM-FATES and needed it. This PR does not change anything in FATES or in the ELM-FATES interface.

<details>
<summary>pytest-dev/pytest (pytest)</summary>

### [`v8.3.5`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/8.3.5)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/8.3.4...8.3.5)

### pytest 8.3.5 (2025-03-02)

#### Bug fixes

-   [#​11777](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11777): Fixed issue where sequences were still being shortened even with `-vv` verbosity.
-   [#​12888](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12888): Fixed broken input when using Python 3.13+ and a `libedit` build of Python, such as on macOS or with uv-managed Python binaries from the `python-build-standalone` project. This could manifest e.g. by a broken prompt when using `Pdb`, or seeing empty inputs with manual usage of `input()` and suspended capturing.
-   [#​13026](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13026): Fixed `AttributeError`{.interpreted-text role="class"} crash when using `--import-mode=importlib` when top-level directory same name as another module of the standard library.
-   [#​13053](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13053): Fixed a regression in pytest 8.3.4 where, when using `--import-mode=importlib`, a directory containing py file with the same name would cause an `ImportError`
-   [#​13083](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13083): Fixed issue where pytest could crash if one of the collected directories got removed during collection.

#### Improved documentation

-   [#​12842](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12842): Added dedicated page about using types with pytest.

    See `types`{.interpreted-text role="ref"} for detailed usage.

#### Contributor-facing changes

-   [#​13112](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13112): Fixed selftest failures in `test_terminal.py` with Pygments >= 2.19.0
-   [#​13256](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13256): Support for Towncrier versions released in 2024 has been re-enabled
    when building Sphinx docs -- by `webknjaz`{.interpreted-text role="user"}.

</details>

:warning: This release contains potential breaking change if you use experimental `zstd` support introduce in [#​1496](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/1496) :warning:

Experimental support for `zstd` on scrape was added, controlled by the request `Accept-Encoding` header.
It was enabled by default since version 1.20, but now you need to add a blank import to enable it.
The decision to make it opt-in by default was originally made because the Go standard library was expected to have default zstd support added soon,
[https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62513](https://redirect.github.com/golang/go/issues/62513) however, the work took longer than anticipated and it will be postponed to upcoming major Go versions.

e.g.:

> ```go
> import (
>   _ "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp/zstd"
> )
> ```

body:
# Implement Dynamic Toolset Discovery

## Overview
This PR implements dynamic toolset discovery in the MCP server, allowing for more efficient tool management and better scalability. Instead of loading all tools at startup, the server now exposes a core set of tools plus special "meta-tools" that enable the client to discover and enable additional toolsets as needed.

## Feature Details
The implementation adds three key tools:
- `list_available_toolsets`: Lists all available groups of tools and their current status
- `get_toolset_tools`: Shows the specific tools available within a given toolset
- `enable_toolset`: Activates a specific toolset, making its tools available for use

## Implementation
The feature is implemented in a new `dynamic` module with the following structure:
- `types.ts`: Type definitions for toolsets and API responses
- `schemas.ts`: Zod schemas for request validation
- `tool-definitions.ts`: Definitions for the dynamic discovery tools
- `index.ts`: Core implementation of toolset management and request handlers
- `index.spec.unit.ts`: Comprehensive unit tests for the feature

Key aspects of the implementation:
```typescript
// Toolset management
export const toolsets = new Map<
  string,
  { description: string; tools: ToolDefinition[]; enabled: boolean }
>();

// Dynamic toolset initialization
export function initializeToolsets(allTools: { [key: string]: ToolDefinition[] }) {
  toolsets.clear();
  // Initialize toolsets with disabled state by default
  Object.entries(allTools).forEach(([name, tools]) => {
    if (name !== 'dynamic') {
      toolsets.set(name, {
        description: `${name} related tools`,
        tools,
        enabled: false,
      });
    }
  });
  // Dynamic toolset is always enabled
  toolsets.set('dynamic', {
    description: 'Tools for discovering and enabling other tools',
    tools: dynamicTools,
    enabled: true,
  });
}
```

## Benefits
- **Improved Performance**: Initial server response is smaller and more manageable
- **Better Resource Usage**: Tools are only loaded when needed
- **Enhanced Flexibility**: LLM can request specific capabilities as needed
- **Cleaner Architecture**: Tools are organized into logical groupings
- **Type Safety**: Full TypeScript type safety throughout the implementation

## Testing
The implementation includes comprehensive unit tests that verify all aspects of the dynamic toolset feature:

### Core Functionality Tests
- **Toolset Initialization**: Verifies correct initial state of toolsets (enabled/disabled status)
- **Dynamic Request Detection**: Ensures proper identification of dynamic tool requests
- **Toolset Management**: Tests the enabling/disabling of toolsets

### Tool-Specific Tests
- **list_available_toolsets**: Validates correct listing of all toolsets with their status
- **get_toolset_tools**: Confirms accurate retrieval of tools within specific toolsets
- **enable_toolset**: Tests successful toolset activation and proper handling of already-enabled toolsets

### Error Handling Tests
- Validates proper error responses for invalid toolset requests
- Tests error handling for unknown dynamic tools
- Ensures appropriate handling of duplicate enable requests

All tests are colocated with the implementation code for better maintainability and are run as part of the unit test suite.

## Example Usage
1. Client requests available tools (`tools/list`)
2. Server responds with core tools + dynamic discovery tools
3. Client discovers additional toolsets via `list_available_toolsets`
4. Client inspects specific toolset via `get_toolset_tools`
5. Client enables desired toolset via `enable_toolset`
6. Newly enabled tools become available in subsequent `tools/list` calls

author: craigmarker
body: Internally, MA Studio query hooks transform Response protobuf messages to provide direct access to the requested data. For example, instead of getting { project: Project } as a response, the hooks provide Project directly. Implemented this functionality for singular-entity endpoints like Get, Create, and Update. Implemented this using UseQueryOptions.select; removed select as an available input to useQuery. This updated the return type of useQuery, which means that the QueryContextType can no longer support a generic that controls the data result. This is because the input Leverage prototobuf-es $typeName property that is included with alongside the generated protobuf client code because it has all the information required for correctly extracting the entity: endpoint name, and entity name. In order to leverage the $typeName property, removed the OmitTypeName wrapper from RpcResponse. $typeName is still removed from RpcRequest. This works well because we don't require clients to provide $typeName but benefit from the server's insertion of the $typeName. **What type of PR is this? import leafmap.maplibregl as leafmap
m = leafmap.Map(use_message_queue=True)

m = leafmap.Map()
```

author: hobbitqia
body:
[Isssue 57](https://github.com/tancheng/VectorCGRA/issues/57) and [Issue 138](https://github.com/tancheng/VectorCGRA/issues/138).

This PR contains 

* A seperate FU for division, which directly implements division through `/`. (`DivRTL.py`)
* An exclusive and inclusive FU for division (`ExclusiveDivRTL.py` and `InclusiveDiveRTL.py`) I implement the division in a pipelined manner in Verilog, and then wrapper the verilog codes in pymtl. The cycle of multi-cycle FU can be configured by the parameter `latency`. For distributed FU, we can just modify the cycles of exclusive FU to reduce hardware cost.

Besides, I have verified that exclusive and inclusive FUs are synthesizable via Vivado.

author: wjdanswjddl
body:
## Description 

This PR includes updates to enable DNN ROI finding, as well as configurations for generating samples for training the DNN. When DNN ROI is enabled, `simtpc2d:dnnsp` (or `sptpc2d:dnnsp` for data) `recob:Wire` products are saved, _in addition to_ the traditional `gauss` and `wiener` products.

For now, the option to run signal processing with DNN ROI is set to false, so this PR shouldn't immediately affect the current workflow in any way. 

Detailed notes on updates:

- `wcls-sim-drift-depoflux-nf-sp.jsonnet`, `wcls-nf-sp-data.jsonnet`, `wcls-nf-sp.jsonnet` were updated to run just the current SP chain using traditional ROI finding workflow by default (`use_dnnroi == false`) and run both traditional and DNN ROI finding SP chains when `use_dnnroi == true`.

- `dnnroi.jsonnet` contains the function to run DNN ROI finding on an APA
    
- `wcsimsp_sbnd.fcl` and `wcsp_data_sbnd.fcl` fcls are updated with DNN ROI specific external variables:
    
    - `use_dnnroi`: option to run SP chain using DNN ROI finding, in addition to the traditional SP chain
    - `nchunks`: number of chunks to divide the wire dimension in for inference, must match the NN training configuration
    - `tick_per_slice`: scale factor for downsampling in the time dimension for inference, must match the NN training configuration
    - `dnnroi_model_p0`, `dnnroi_model_p1`: path to NN file, to be stored in `/cvmfs/sbnd.opensciencegrid.org/products/sbnd/sbnd_data/<version>/WireCell`, which is on $WIRECELL_PATH.
- `cafmakerjob_sbnd.fcl`,  `cafmakerjob_sbnd_data_base.fcl`, `standard_detsim_sbnd.fcl`, `standard_reco1_sbnd.fcl`, `reco1_data.fcl`, were updated with commented lines that can be uncommented to run the workflow with DNN ROI finding, using the `dnnsp` product.
    
- `wcls-sim-drift-depoflux-nf-sp-samples_{tru,rec}.jsonnet`, `wirecell_sim_{tru,rec}.fcl`: jsonnets and fcls for generating training samples

author: poplexity
body:
DON'T MERGE UNTIL #44 IS MERGED

- EVM voting
- Vote decay
- Scaled BP pay
- Self-stake boost

This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the Telos system contract to support EVM-based voting and related configuration, as well as improvements to the voting mechanism. The main changes include new data structures and tables for EVM voting, several new contract actions for managing voting configuration and synchronizing BP (block producer) status with the EVM, and the integration of new libraries for EVM and Ethereum compatibility. These updates enable on-chain management of EVM voting parameters, retrieval and normalization of EVM votes, and synchronization of BP status between EOSIO and EVM.

**EVM Voting Integration and Configuration**

* Added new tables: `evm_vote_info` and `evm_votes_table` to store EVM vote data for block producers, and `votingconfig_singleton` to hold EVM voting contract configuration and decay parameters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R459-R462) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820L465-R545)
* Integrated new external libraries (`eosio.evm`, `intx`, `rlp`) for EVM compatibility and cryptographic operations, updating CMake and includes accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f4ca0ba1c9b5f5cd1f6c69c058b2b429e2cb07339882f5bf81f2c4cc4d8da91L28-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70R7-R14) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R20) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R49)

**New Contract Actions for Voting Management**

* Added actions: `setvotedecay`, `setvotecontr`, `getevmvote`, `setbpevmstat`, and `setselfstake` for configuring EVM voting parameters, updating BP status in EVM, and managing self-stake boost multipliers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R1702-R1726) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70R566-R805)
* Exposed these actions via action wrappers for external invocation.

**State Management and Initialization**

* Updated contract constructors and state management to initialize and persist new voting configuration and EVM votes tables. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70L38-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70R59) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70R91) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R930-R932)

**Voting Logic Extensions**

* Added new helper functions for vote weight decay and conversion between uint256 and double, supporting more nuanced voting calculations.

(EVM integration: [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R459-R462) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820L465-R545) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2f4bad21e70a5e052748173b2e516f8006a41379299ad5a19b77aebe89b9c820R930-R932) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d6dbe33f03defb6e34b39d8d582c0b98c296de2b6b038230b0dc1aa1bbdd4e70R566-R805)

author: ybkimdev
body:
## Description
- Dummy Server 추가 (BE Server 없을 때, 테스트 할 용도)
- .env에 ENVIRONMENT 옵션이 dev로 되어 있을때 dummy server를 활성화 하도록 되어 있고, ai_process에서 dummy server의 IP (localhost-127.0.0.1)로 요청을 보내게 개발 함.
- ai_process.py에 requests 요청을 보내는 곳과 ModerationResultRequest 클래스 필드 일부 문서 기준으로 수정
- moderation_controller.py에 테스트용 API 추가 (api/v1/moderation/test)
- Router 별로 Tag 설정

## How to run
1. `.env`를 `.env.example` 파일과 동일하게 구성하고 ENVIRONMENT를 dev로 설정.
2. `python app.py` 실행

author: pinkbat5
body:
<!-- Impstation note: there's no need to read all the official contributing guidelines,
but please DON'T combine upstream changes with your own changes.
Make separate pull requests for separate changes. -->
<!-- Guidelines: https://docs.spacestation14.io/en/getting-started/pr-guideline -->
Combination of guidebook and roundstart "you answer to..." message changes to make the Head of Personnel the official second in command for the station.
Reasoning:
-HoP is no longer the head of the service department and needs a new niche and set of responsibilities.
-HoPs usually have more free time on their hands than captains. In my own personal experience, if a member of command mistreats an employee, there's no recourse because the captain is too busy to talk to them. HoP doesn't have this problem, and it makes sense for them to be the "HR"/conflict resolution guy.
-Pairs well with https://github.com/impstation/imp-station-14/pull/2380, which makes the lawyer the HoP's direct subordinate. This allows the lawyer to run crying to the HoP in the event that they are ignored by security (a common issue), and the HoP now has the explicit authority to tell security to listen.
-Second in commands are cool.

I'm not fully convinced of this change myself. I do enjoy some of the interactions that emerge from HoPs and other members of command being on equal footing, neither having direct authority over the other, and the uncertainty that can cause. But maybe this will also be interesting? I think this is a worth a try. We can always change it back.

I also removed all guidebook references to the HoP being in charge of service. We desperately need a Research Director figurine for guidebook usage.

**Changelog**
<!-- Impstation note: we have our own AUTOMATIC changelog now, so please DO use this section! -->
<!-- Add a Changelog entry to make players aware of new features or changes that could affect gameplay.
Make sure to read the guidelines and take this Changelog template out of the comment block in order for it to show up.
Changelog must have a :cl: symbol, so the bot recognizes the changes and adds them to the game's changelog. -->

:cl:
- tweak: The Head of Personnel is now the second in command of the station. Act accordingly!
- fix: Removed guidebook references to the HoP as the head of the service department.

  3. Semantic line-based chunking
  4. Basic line-based chunking (fallback)

- Add graceful degradation for missing dependencies
- Update configuration to support flexible chunking strategy selection
- Add detailed logging and error handling for chunker initialization
- Update documentation in memory-bank and README

body:
## Why did you make these changes?

https://deakinuniversity.atlassian.net/browse/CON-2610
https://deakinuniversity.atlassian.net/browse/CON-2611

## What changes did you make?

Firstly, use the correct `viewport-fit` in the HTML `viewport` metadata so that it renders within the full screen within the mobile apps. Then needed to set some additional CSS to ensure the canvas was drawn correctly to the bottom of the screen in iOS.

Next I set the game configuration to `scale { mode: Phaser.Scale.RESIZE }` to fit all available space in the window, and set the game width and height to the windows width and height. This of course caused a number of components to no longer fit correctly. So these had to be fixed up to ensure they dynamically size (like the power-meter and progress bars), and position panels correctly.

The manual resize function has been removed as it is no longer needed, and if you did resize the window it would not correctly adjust the game anyway. And I removed the decision point sign as well.

## TODO

There's a couple screens where the positioning of items is not yet perfect, which I'll address seperately; caused when the screen is too narrow, and status bar covering the progress bar in the mobile apps.

This pull request introduces significant updates to model support, configuration handling, and tool management, along with some improvements to error reporting. Key changes include expanding model integrations, refining configuration options, and adding functionality for dynamically registering and managing tools.

### Model Support Enhancements:
* Updated the `README.md` to reflect support for new models, including OpenAI's `GPT-4.1` and `GPT-4.1-mini`, Google's `Gemini 2.5` series, and Anthropic's `Claude 3.7 Sonnet`. Removed references to deprecated models like PaLM and older Gemini versions.
* Added new model configurations in `config.js` for `oai-gpt41`, `oai-gpt41-mini`, `claude-35-sonnet-vertex`, and `gemini-flash-20-vision`, with parameters for API endpoints, headers, and token limits. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR229-R258) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR369-R391)

### Configuration Improvements:
* Introduced new configuration options in `config.js`, such as `claudeVertexUrl`, `geminiFlashUrl`, and `entityConfig`, to support additional models and entities.
* Implemented logic to merge and preserve default entity configurations, ensuring a default entity is always set. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR489-R491) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR507-R527)

### Tool Management:
* Enhanced pathway tools by dynamically registering tools from pathway definitions in `config.js`. Tools are validated for duplicates and missing fields, and added to a centralized registry (`entityTools`).
* Added a new `callTool` function in `lib/pathwayTools.js` to execute tools dynamically, handle search results, and support pathway-based tool execution.
* Exported the `callTool` function for external use.

### Error Reporting:
* Improved error messages in `lib/requestExecutor.js` by including detailed response data when available, making debugging easier.

### Deprecations and Cleanups:
* Removed outdated model configurations for PaLM chat and completion models from `config/default.example.json`.This pull request introduces significant enhancements to model support, configuration management, and tool integration, along with updates to error handling for improved debugging. The most important changes include adding new AI models, updating configuration defaults, enhancing tool registration and execution, and improving error messages for HTTP requests.

### Model and Configuration Enhancements:
* Updated `README.md` to reflect new model support, including GPT-4.1 (+mini, +nano), Gemini 2.5 series, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet, while removing outdated entries such as PaLM chat models. Added Ollama support.
* Added new configuration defaults in `config.js` for `claudeVertexUrl`, `geminiFlashUrl`, and `entityConfig`. Introduced `entityTools` to manage tools registry. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR93-R137) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR489-R491)
* Added model definitions for GPT-4.1 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet Vertex in `config.js`, enabling advanced features like streaming and extended token limits. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR229-R258) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e8e9eea3276b2de9a74fd257902dc74c846f6fc8653bbddf45d738b71201f93dR369-R391)

### Tool Integration:
* Introduced `callTool` function in `lib/pathwayTools.js` for executing tools with enhanced error handling, support for pathway-specific parameters, and search result accumulation.
* Registered tools dynamically in `config.js` based on pathway definitions, ensuring proper validation and avoiding duplicate registrations.

### Error Handling Improvements:
* Enhanced HTTP error messages in `lib/requestExecutor.js` to include detailed response data for easier debugging.

These changes collectively improve the functionality, maintainability, and extensibility of the system.

author: agjharms
body:
In this pull request the Health-RI model is updated to support the metadata model Health-RI v2-rc1, in preparation for the release of the Health-RI v2 model. 

Compared to the previous pre-release model of the Health-RI v2 model, the Project and Study classes have been removed.

## Summary by Sourcery

Update Health-RI model to support v2-rc1 metadata model, removing Project and Study classes and making various refinements to the data model

New Features:
- Added support for applicable legislation in datasets
- Enhanced flexibility in metadata field definitions

Enhancements:
- Removed Project and Study classes
- Updated field descriptions to be more generic
- Made some previously mandatory fields optional
- Improved type handling for various fields

Chores:
- Refactored model definitions across multiple files
- Updated test cases to reflect model changes
- Removed deprecated or redundant code

author: kremalicious
body:
This pull request introduces several updates to the project, including enhancements to CI workflows, improvements to test coverage, and updates to build configurations. The key changes involve adding a new type-checking step to the CI pipeline, restructuring and expanding test cases, and refining build scripts for better maintainability and output.

### CI Workflow Enhancements:
* Added a new `typecheck` job to the CI workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, ensuring TypeScript type-checking is performed on `ubuntu-latest` with Node.js 22.

### Build and Configuration Updates:
* Updated the `build` script in `package.json` to use `tsconfig.build.json` for more specific build configurations.
* Introduced a new `tsconfig.build.json` file to define build-specific TypeScript options, including output directories and declaration file generation.
* Removed the `validate` script and associated dependencies from `package.json`, simplifying the script structure.

### Test Suite Improvements:
* Added new test cases in `test/build.test.ts` to validate build output, ensuring all expected files and types are generated correctly.
* Refactored and expanded tests for `getRedirects` in `test/getRedirects.test.ts`, including new cases for handling invalid redirects, unexpected types, and error logging.
* Renamed `test/redirects.test.ts` to `test/createRedirect.test.ts` and removed unrelated test cases to focus solely on `createRedirect`.
* Updated `test/index.test.ts` to include additional scenarios for `initPlugin` and `astroRedirectFrom`, improving coverage for custom options and error handling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ec61822d929089017a892b4b047229377c9241f16b43252ab851ae39131cdf40L76-R126) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec61822d929089017a892b4b047229377c9241f16b43252ab851ae39131cdf40L102-R149)

### Documentation Updates:
* Removed the `npm run test:unit` command from the `README.md` as it is no longer part of the scripts, aligning the documentation with the updated `package.json`.

body:
This PR adds support for handling RARed RealDebrid torrents - cases where RD packages multiple files into a single RAR archive download link. This implementation allows for downloading individual files within archives without spending the bandwidth to download the entire archive.

**What's New:**

- Go port of [RARAR.py](https://github.com/eliasbenb/RARAR.py) which allows for random access to RAR archives
- Updated RealDebrid's torrent handler to detect RAR archives
- Enabled byte range tracking for RARed files
- The downloader and streamer now automatically apply RAR byte ranges

author: reunanen
body:
I am using `InflatePaths`, and I had the following problem that took a long time to figure out:

**Background**

The `Group` constructor currently needs to figure out if exteriors are clockwise and holes are counter-clockwise, or the other way around. It accomplishes this by finding the lowest path (=the one having the highest _y_ coordinate), because that must be an outer path, and by checking if its area is positive or negative.

**Problem**

Now if the lowest path contains only 1 or 2 points, or otherwise has zero area, and the paths are indeed "reversed", then the above logic does not work as intended.

It wouldn't be a problem to simply drop such degenerate paths, but the issue is that if the same group contains also non-degenerate, large, significant paths, they may effectively be dropped as well. This is exactly what was sometimes happening in my use case. (Just for the record, my workaround was to weed such degenerate paths from the input, before calling `InflatePaths`. Very easy once I knew what exactly the problem was, but to get to that point took quite a while...)

(Where would such degenerate paths come from? I think for example from calling OpenCV's [`findContours`](https://docs.opencv.org/4.11.0/d3/dc0/group__imgproc__shape.html#gadf1ad6a0b82947fa1fe3c3d497f260e0) for 1- or 2-pixel regions.)

**What this PR does**

This PR just adds an `assert` that should detect if the input data is such that the logic can't really work as intended. Having this available would have saved me a lot of time, so I thought it might help others who may be providing similar input data. Generally `assert`s are no-op in Release builds, so Release builds should remain unaffected. Alternatively, one could throw a `std::logic_error` or similar, but I guess that doing so would be more intrusive and might break applications that are currently working (although they would be "working" only if the paths are _not_ reversed).

**Alternative solutions**

For clarity, I think it might be best to let the user explicitly provide the orientation also in the offset case (similar to the "main" clipping functionality, such as intersection), instead of trying to figure it out from the input data. (Should be a tad faster, too?)

Another alternative would be to find the lowest path that _has non-zero area_ (instead of just the lowest path).

Angus, if you like either of the above suggestions, I can try and prepare an alternative PR.

**Unrelated remark**

(There is also a cosmetic spaces vs tabs issue here in this location, but I tried to keep the diff minimal and not start fixing that, at least for the time being.)

author: brandonpollack23
body:
First in a series of changes to add scalar returns to method calls in providers.

The code for a scalar value in the schema (pcl spec) already exists for
the ReturnType field, this change adds the nodejs sdk and codegen
required to leverage that.

When it is all done it will work like so:

    1. Sdk was modified to have symmetric calls to the invoke* family of functions which handle returning single/scalar or objects as either output or plain values (promise).
    1. Codegen detects the type of ReturnType field is not ObjectType, and
    generates the appropriate sdk api code for the function call to
    return a scalar.
    1. Single keyed PropertyMaps are returned from the provider for the
       scalar.
    1. The generated code appropriately unmarshals the single value and
       returns from the call in the program's sdk code.

This PR is sdk only and will require a release before the programgen
code ships.

Part of #7435

author: skshamkaushal
body:
### **PR Type** Enhancement, Bug fix, Documentation, Other ___ ### **Description** - Added new POST API endpoints for creating users and workouts, including error handling and integration into the Express server. - Standardized the `User` model's gender enum values and export naming. - Upgraded `mongoose` and `mongodb` dependencies to latest versions, updating related type definitions and scripts for improved coverage and compatibility. - Enhanced Mongoose typings for virtuals, middleware, bulk operations, and schema options. - Improved MongoDB driver error handling, message parsing, and added support for the `hint` option in distinct operations. - Fixed bulk write concern error code to use `WriteConcernTimeout` for more accurate error reporting. - Updated documentation to clarify deprecations and new/changed options in both MongoDB and Mongoose. - Updated various source map files to reflect changes in the underlying TypeScript sources. ___ ### **Changes walkthrough** 📝
Relevant files
Enhancement
20 files
User.js
Standardize gender enum and model export naming in User schema
backend/models/User.js
  • Changed the enum values for gender from single quotes to double
    quotes.
  • Updated the model export name from 'user' to 'User'.
  • Minor whitespace adjustment in the name field.
    		• +3/-3     
    userRoutes.js
    Add user creation POST API route with error handling         
    backend/routes/userRoutes.js
  • Added a new Express router for user-related routes.
  • Implemented a POST endpoint /saveUser to create and save a new user.
  • Handles errors and returns appropriate JSON responses.
  • Imports the User and Workout models.
    		• +31/-0   
    workoutRoutes.js
    Add workout creation POST API route with error handling   
    backend/routes/workoutRoutes.js
  • Added a new Express router for workout-related routes.
  • Implemented a POST endpoint /saveWorkout to create and save a new
    workout.
  • Handles errors and returns appropriate JSON responses.
  • Imports the User and Workout models.
    		• +27/-0   
    server.js
    Integrate user and workout API routes and improve server messaging
    backend/server.js
  • Added middleware to use the new user and workout routes under
    /api/users and /api/workouts.
  • Improved the root route response message.
  • Updated the server start log message for clarity.
    		• +9/-3     
    index.d.ts
    Improve Mongoose typings for virtuals and middleware         
    backend/node_modules/mongoose/types/index.d.ts
  • Enhanced type definitions for HydratedDocument and related types to
    better support virtuals and query helpers.
  • Added support for specifying virtuals in toJSON and toObject methods.
  • Added a new overload for the pre middleware for the init event.
    		• +12/-8   
    inferrawdoctype.d.ts
    Enhance raw doc type inference for arrays in Mongoose       
    backend/node_modules/mongoose/types/inferrawdoctype.d.ts
  • Improved type inference for array fields in schema definitions.
  • Replaced usage of ObtainDocumentType with InferRawDocType for better
    raw type inference.
  • Fixed documentation to reference ResolveRawPathType.
    		• +7/-7     
    document.d.ts
    Add virtuals support to Document typings in Mongoose         
    backend/node_modules/mongoose/types/document.d.ts
  • Added a generic parameter for virtuals to the Document class.
  • Added overloads for toJSON and toObject to support returning virtuals.
    		• +3/-1     
    connection.ts
    Refactor message parsing and error handling in SizedMessageTransform
    backend/node_modules/mongodb/src/cmap/connection.ts
  • Refactored the SizedMessageTransform to process multiple messages in a
    single chunk.
  • Improved error handling for negative message sizes and backpressure.
  • Added use of MongoRuntimeError for unsupported backpressure scenarios.
    		• +31/-11 
    connection.d.ts
    Add connection-level bulkWrite typings to Mongoose             
    backend/node_modules/mongoose/types/connection.d.ts
  • Added new types for bulk write models at the connection level.
  • Introduced bulkWrite method to the Connection class with improved
    typings.
    		• +22/-0   
    mongodb.d.ts
    Add hint option to DistinctOptions and clarify update event docs
    backend/node_modules/mongodb/mongodb.d.ts
  • Extended DistinctOptions to include a hint property for index

## Summary

Introduces full support for editing Points of Interest (POIs) from the admin panel. It includes a new AdminEditPOI.vue view with dynamic form rendering, form validation, and localization support. POI data is fetched from the backend and can be updated or deleted with confirmation prompts. Also includes translation additions, styling adjustments, and an update to the admin dashboard to access POI editing.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
Create a temporary ClientSession early in case we need to load version information from the internet. This doesn't use the final DNS setup and hence might fail to load in certain situations since we don't have the fallback mechanims in place yet. But if the DNS container image is present, we'll continue the setup and load the DNS plug-in. We then can recreate the ClientSession such that it uses the DNS plug-in.

This works around an issue with aiodns, which today doesn't reload `resolv.conf` automatically when it changes. This lead to Supervisor using the initial `resolv.conf` as created by Docker. It meant that we did not use the DNS plug-in (and its fallback capabilities) in Supervisor. Also it meant that changes to the DNS setup at runtime did not propagate to the aiohttp ClientSession (as observed in #5332).

See [DTSPO-24115](https://tools.hmcts.net/jira/browse/DTSPO-24115)

### Change description

<!--
Provide a description of what change you are proposing.
A short summary here and then you can add comments in your pull request explaining your change to others.
-->
This PR introduces the capability to remove the Splunk Universal Forwarder (UF) as part of the VM bootstrap process, facilitating its decommissioning.

Key changes include:
*   Added a new Terraform variable `remove_splunk_uf` (defaulting to `true`) to control the removal action.
*   Updated `locals.tf` to pass this new variable to the bootstrap scripts.
*   Modified the Linux bootstrap script (`bootstrap_vm.sh`):
    *   Added logic to check for and remove Splunk UF if `remove_splunk_uf` is true. This includes stopping the service, disabling boot-start, and removing files. The script checks if Splunk exists before attempting removal to avoid errors.
    *   Removed logic to install Splunk, whilst keeping the `install_splunk_uf` variable so as not to break anything reliant on it.
*   Updated `custom_script.tf`: Modified the `count` logic for the Custom Script Extension resources to ensure the bootstrap script runs if `remove_splunk_uf` is true, even if `install_splunk_uf` is false.

author: bprashanth
body:
Previously we were sliding the tiling window across the entire orthomosaic. This had the undesired effect of producing many completely empty/mostly empty tiles, which would have confused the training phase and potentially resulted in labelling bias (the model would have started looking for empties and treating transparent edges as an indicator of lantana growth).

In order to avoid this, we:
1. Figure out what the "nodata" value is from the dataset (rasterio exposes a `read_mask` function that returns this value)
2. This is a mask of the entire source. This mask shows 1 for "contains pixel" and 0 for "nodata". In some cases it might record "transparent" for nodata, but this is irrelevant.
3. Clip this mask to the bounds of the current sliding window.
4. Compute the % of nodata vs data pixels in the current window and compare against `--skip_threshold`.
5. If the tile is eg less than 10% real pixels (which is the default value of skip_threshold), discard it.

To revert this behavior, set `--skip_threshold` to `0`, which means even 0 valid data pixels will not result in skipping the tile. To only skip competely empty tiles, set it to a small value like `0.001`.

author: blacktanktoplab
body:
## Summary
This PR extends the plot_protein_backbone function to support visualization of cyclic peptides by explicitly connecting the N-terminal and C-terminal atoms in the rendering logic.

## Motivation
Cyclic peptides form a covalent bond between the N-terminus and C-terminus, which was not previously visualized in plot_protein_backbone. This led to incomplete backbone representations for such structures. Supporting cyclic peptide visualization improves the accuracy and interpretability of rendered backbone plots in cases involving head-to-tail cyclization.

author: mathieudutsik
body:
## Motivation

The versions of alloy used in examples/Cargo.toml and Cargo.toml had diverged and needed to be reunified.
Also the `alloy-signer-local` was unused and needed to be removed.

## Proposal

Both changes are done.

The elimination of `alloy-signer-local` is more important than it looks like. Version 0.9.2 depends on `c-kzg`.
Unfortunately, version 22.0.1 of REVM depends on `c-kzg` as well and a native library can be present only
one time in the linking process.

In other words, one block for the use of the next version of Revm has been cleared. Two more obstacles remain:
* The resolution of the issue https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/issues/2425
* The upgrade of Revm from version 22.0.1 to the next one with this bug correction and the change of the PR https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/pull/2464

When this is done, we could finally use Linera ApplicationId (the 20 bytes long version of course) in EVM contracts.

## Test Plan

The CI.

## Release Plan

- Nothing to do / These changes follow the usual release cycle.

Removes `css.preprocessorOptions.{sass,scss}.api` option and always use `'modern-compiler'` for it.

Currently, search engines don't know which version to show for API documentation. For example, searching for "ruby string" in Google will show the documentation for Ruby 2.0 `https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/2.0.0/String.html` as the top result (for docs.ruby-lang.org).

The canonical URL link tag will allow us to set the preferred version:

> The canonical URL link tag defines the preferred URL for the current
> document, which helps search engines reduce duplicate content.

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/rel#canonical

For example, for the official Ruby documentation we can add the following to `.rdoc_options`.

```yaml
canonical_root: https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master
```

This will add the canonical URL link tag to relevant pages:

```html
<link rel="canonical" href="https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/String.html">
```

author: sjpb
body:
Fixes issues preventing updating the appliance version used for Azimuth caas clusters:


1. 502 error when trying to connect to monitoring/ondemand:

    RockyLinux 9.5 upgraded to podman v5, which changes the default rootless network tool from slirp4netns to pasta. 
    The latter doesn't allow containers to reach the host's IP - see https://blog.podman.io/2024/03/podman-5-0-breaking-changes-in-detail/. This PR reverts the network stack for the zenith pod to slirp4netns[^1]. It has been tested on RL9.5 only in caas. However the same option is supported in podman v4.9 used by RockyLinux 8.10 so this seems safe.

    It also bumps the container images for the zenith clients and proxies, and removes some now-unneeded zenith configuration.


2. The "post-configuration validation" (hpctests) fails:

        hpctests : Create test root directory: 
        There was an issue creating /home/rocky as requested: [Errno 13] Permission denied: b'/home/rocky'

    The issue is that since https://github.com/stackhpc/ansible-slurm-appliance/pull/599, `become` when running on the login node can't be used to create directories in /home. Therefore the `hpctests_user` is set to `azimuth`. Note #663 was also required (merged from main).

3. https://github.com/stackhpc/ansible-slurm-appliance/pull/599 changed configuration for the `basic_users` role, to cope with root-squashed NFS shares. The appliance defaults are suitable for that case, so need conditional modifications for the manila case. To make this simplier, caas slurm now mounts `/home` on the control node when manila is in use, which makes it consistent with NFS, and will now mean the `azimuth` user can access the control node whichever home fileshare is in use.

No image build is required for any of these changes.

[^1]: An alternative option may be to use pasta with the `--map-gw` option, but https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/22771 suggests this only works properly from podman v5.1, and it is not clear without testing that the gateway address = host's "main" IP address. Therefore simply restoring the previous behaviour seems preferable at the moment.

This starts with reverting #39 because [it's broken](https://github.com/OpenVoxProject/puppet/pull/39#issuecomment-2840341655) and caused a regression. Then   I've taken my commits from https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppet/pull/9546.

Ruby 3.4 started error checking directory access and starts to raise Errno::EBADF.

This particular loop iterates on all open file descriptors and one is the directory listing from Dir.foreach.

In the past this could have led to leaked file descriptors, but it's unlikely since it's likely the last opened file descriptor and have the highest number.

Link: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/commit/f2919bd11c570fc5f5440d1f101be38f61e3d16b
Link: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2349352

author: dhfra21
body:
## Problem

The `NumberField` component was not displaying small decimal values correctly. By default, it was truncating or rounding very small numbers (e.g., 0.0001) to 0, which could lead to data loss and incorrect representation of values. This was particularly problematic for scientific, financial, or precise measurements where small decimal values are important.

## Solution

I've modified the `NumberField` component to set a default `maximumFractionDigits` value of 100 in the options object. This ensures that small decimal values are displayed with their full precision by default. The change is implemented in a way that:

1. Preserves backward compatibility
2. Allows users to override the default behavior if needed
3. Maintains the existing formatting capabilities for other number types (currencies, percentages, etc.)


## How To Test

1. Create a record with a small decimal value:  `const record = { id: 1, value: 0.0001 };`
2. Render the NumberField component:  `<NumberField source="value" record={record} />`
3. Verify that the small decimal value is displayed correctly as "0.0001"
4. Test overriding the default behavior: ```
<NumberField 
    source="value" 
    record={record} 
    options={{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }} 
/>

author: landrian61
body:
This pull request introduces several significant changes to enhance Firebase integration, improve server architecture, and add new functionality for public farm location access. Key updates include transitioning Firebase initialization to support both production and development environments, adding a new public API endpoint for farm locations, and restructuring notification handling for better error management.

### Firebase Integration Enhancements:
* Moved Firebase initialization logic to a new `firebaseInit.js` utility, supporting both base64-encoded service accounts for production and local service account files for development. This ensures flexibility across environments (`utils/firebaseAdmin.js`, `utils/firebaseInit.js`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-17ba320c75da8688e512f433c8e458a3bc182401301a097b3db52b146b88443bL1-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6576c2798636abe572bd8ace0bc9596ff2b37398844dd0bc4d072a22b80a99ffR1-R83)
* Updated the `.env` file to include a base64-encoded Firebase service account key for secure production use (`.env`).
* Upgraded the `firebase-admin` package to version `11.11.1` for compatibility with the new initialization approach (`package.json`).

### Public Farm Location API:
* Added a new public endpoint `/public-farm-locations` in `mapRoutes.js` to allow unauthenticated access to verified farmers' location and environmental data. This includes logic to fetch and aggregate the latest environmental data for each farmer (`routes/mapRoutes.js`).

### Server and Middleware Improvements:
* Introduced a new `app.js` file to centralize Express server setup, including middleware configuration and route mounting. This modularizes the server code for better maintainability (`app.js`).
* Adjusted CORS configuration in `server.js` to include a new local IP address for development purposes (`server.js`).

### Notification Service Updates:
* Enhanced the push notification logic to handle Firebase initialization errors gracefully and log detailed information about failed tokens. Added a helper function to remove invalid device tokens from the database (`utils/notificationService.js`).

### Miscellaneous:
* Added a new Firebase service account JSON file for local development (`config/serviceAccountKey.json`).
* Refactored imports in `server.js` to use the new `firebaseInit.js` utility (`server.js`).

author: cardopixel
body:
feat: Add Google AI API integration for Gemini models

## Feature Description

This pull request introduces support for access to Gemini LLM models using [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com), a paid and proprietary tool owned by Google. This changes integrates to the project the necessary changes to enable seamless integration of Gemini models (paid and with 'free' tier) within the Godot AI Assistant Hub Plugin.

## Motivation

The primary motivation is to provide a fully functional AI assistant solution directly within Godot v4 leveraging the power of Gemini models provided by Google. This allows developers to with low spec machines use a large context in the prompts and receive fast and accurate responses, hopefully solving many questions/problems during development. 

## Key Changes

    - Creates `addons/ai_assistant_hub/llm_apis/gemini_api.gd` implementing the `LLMInterface` for Gemini, including methods for fetching models, sending chat requests, and parsing responses.
    - Implements API key management for Gemini, allowing the key to be stored in Project Settings or a dedicated `gemini_api_key.gd` file for better security and persistence.
    - Introduces `_init_gemini_api_key` function to load/save the API key on editor startup.
    - Updates `addons/ai_assistant_hub/ai_hub_plugin.gd`:     
       - Adds configuration constant `CONFIG_GEMINI_API_KEY`.          
       - Includes "Gemini" in the list returned by `get_available_llm_providers`.     
       - Enhances `new_llm_provider` to gracefully handle errors if an LLM provider script fails to load. 
    - Updates `addons/ai_assistant_hub/ai_chat.gd`:     
       - Adds checks in `load_api` and `_submit_prompt` to ensure the `_llm` provider is successfully loaded before use, preventing potential errors. 
    - Updates `addons/ai_assistant_hub/llm_apis/llm_interface.gd`:     
       - Improves JSON parsing error handling in `get_full_response`.

## Testing

The integration was tested on the following configuration:

- **Operating System:** Windows 10 Pro build 19045.5737
- **Hardware:** Lenovo ThinkPad L14 Gen1 AMD Ryzen 3 Pro 4450U with Radeon Graphics (2Gb shared VRAM), 16Gb of DDR4 RAM.
- **Software:**
    - Godot v4.4 Stable
    - Jan v0.5.16
    - Models: [gemini-2.0-flash](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/flash/), [gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/flash/)

Testing focused on simple requests, such as generating code-based state machines and performing minor refactoring tasks on existing scripts. More complex scenarios may require further testing.

## Additional Notes

- The Gemini API integration assumes a the user have a Google AI Studio API Key.
- Further testing and refinement may be needed to ensure compatibility with a wider range of models of Gemini and other Google AI based models.

author: idriss-malek
body:
This pull request adds support for using custom rewards in GFlowNet implementations, enabling the use of intrinsic rewards for example (https://openreview.net/forum?id=HH4KWP8RP5).

## Changes

- Added a `log_rewards` argument to GFlowNet implementations.
  - By default, it is set to `None`, in which case the environment's reward is used. This preserves compatibility with existing code.
  - When provided, `log_rewards` is expected to be a tensor of the same shape as the container (e.g., `(n_trajectories,)`, `(n_transitions,)`, etc.), and it's used instead of the environment reward.

- In the DB and SubTB losses, I did not modify the forward-looking setup, except to rename the argument to `fl_log_rewards` to avoid naming conflicts.
  - I am not sure what this forward-looking setup does exactly (would appreciate any pointers to the original reference).
  - For now, I recommend using custom rewards with caution when using the forward-looking setup.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/manyfold3d/manyfold/compare/v0.108.1...v0.109.0)

Some new features for admins in this release, and some metadata parse and import improvements!

There is now a `bin/manyfold` command that can do various admin tasks, like cleaning up incorrect data; the [Advanced Tasks](https://manyfold.app/sysadmin/advanced_tasks.html) page on the website explains how to use it.  You can now also set an upload quota for accounts, handy if you're running a public instance. You can set a site-wide default, then override it for each account individually.

Metdata parsing has been improved and made more reliable; "rescan all models" in the menu and "rescan all files" in a single model both now do the same thing, and will re-parse metadata from path templates and other sources. A new source for metadata is README files; they're now read into the model description automatically, but if it's a Thingiverse-formatted README, we also automatically try to set creator, title, and license.

author: buhtz
body:
Fix #714
Fix #1090

This might fix most of the systems. But there might be still some rare combinations of Linux and DE versions and their DBus services they do provide for power management.

### Tests
**Successful** tests:

* Debian GNU/Linux 12 (stable) (native on hardware)
  * Xfce: `freedesktop.login1` (system bus)
  * KDE Plasma Wayland: `freedesktop.login1` (system bus)
  * Cinnamon: `freedesktop.login1` (system bus)
* Devuan GNU/Linux 5 (based on Debian 12)
  * Xfce: `freedesktop.login1` (system bus)

Tests with **errors**:
* None

Tests with **other problems**:
* Gnome on Debian, did not suspend the monitor because of several other inhibitors.

### Details
BIT now try to use the system bus and the "login1" method first. This is the standard on most modern systems, even without systemd. And this DBus provider does distinguish between suspend and idle.

The reason for the original problem was that the gnome/cinnamon session bus was used. Additional the idle flag was used, too. But even without the idle flag the monitor woke up. It depends on how the DBus provider is implemented. Some does ignore the flags, handle them different, even if they share the same API. You'll never know for sure.

body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

Resolve [Implement /eth/v1/node/peers/{peer_id} #222](https://github.com/ReamLabs/ream/issues/222)

### How was it implemented/fixed?

- **New route** – Added `GET /node/peers/{peer_id}` to align with the beacon-node API spec.  
- **Input validation** – `peer_id` is parsed with `libp2p::PeerId::from_str`; invalid IDs fail fast with `ApiError::BadRequest`.  
- **Response shape** – Returns JSON-wrapped `PeerData`  
  ```json
  {
    "peer_id": "<peer_id>",
    "enr": null,
    "last_seen_p2p_address": "<p2p_address>",
    "state": "connected",
    "direction": "outbound"
  }

- **Error handling** – Parsing and lookup errors map to `ApiError::{BadRequest, NotFound, InternalError}` and are logged via `tracing` for easier debugging.  
- **Stub data source** – Introduced `mock_fetch_peer` as a temporary stand-in; it supplies hard-coded peer info while we wire up the real `Network` integration.

#### Example request

```bash
curl -X GET -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:5052/eth/v1/node/peers/16Uiu2HAmUaM4YkWtwpu6P299nZuDwTCyUsrXeArCynSS1irSjXAM
```

<details> <summary>Sample response</summary>

```json
{
  "data": {
    "peer_id": "16Uiu2HAm1oEch6uXffoGZ32kPTiyjycfX9yDuBJSWtmagBSk9HTN",
    "enr": null,
    "last_seen_p2p_address": "/ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/9000/p2p/16Uiu2HAm1oEch6uXffoGZ32kPTiyjycfX9yDuBJSWtmagBSk9HTN",
    "state": "connected",
    "direction": "outbound"
  }
}
```
</details> 

### To-Do

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ReamLabs/ream/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] This PR uses [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).
- [x] Confirm that `PeerData` must be fetched directly from `p2p/src/network.rs::Network` (not from the database) for the `/node/peers/{peer_id}` endpoint.
- [x] Implement a read function (e.g., `fn cached_peer(&self, id: &PeerId) -> Option<CachedPeer>`) in `p2p/src/network.rs` to expose live peer data to the RPC layer.
- [x] Inject `Arc<Network>` into the RPC server (`start_server`) and register it with `App::app_data` so that handlers can call `network.cached_peer(...)`.

author: natebeauregard
body:
fixes https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/issues/13883

The validator client, when asked to attest to a proposal, first checks that all txs are available on the tx pool and then loads them as needed. However, between these two calls, the p2p mempool (if full) may have chosen to evict some of these txs, meaning the validator will not have the txs it needs. This race condition may also happen during any process that loops requesting txs (e.g. prover coordination).

This PR adds a way to instruct the p2p mempool to not evict txs that are going to be needed soon and calls it right before any process that starts collecting txs (re-execution or proving). After the request is done, the txs are marked as evictable again.

author: samy-00007
body:
GCC uses the `%=` syntax to generate a unique number for each `asm` statement (see [on gcc's docs](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Extended-Asm.html#Special-format-strings)). LLVM uses `${:uid}` to do the same.

This PR adds the syntax, since it is not currently possible to use `%=` or `${:uid}` in zig's inline assembly. Also, it is currently impossible to use `${:comment}` or `${:private}` described [here on llvm's docs](https://releases.llvm.org/10.0.0/docs/LangRef.html#inline-assembler-expressions), and this PR does **not** change that.

I am unsure if this change requires tests, and how to even test it.

author: sjrd
body:
And make its internals independent of JS interop.
This way, it will be usable in Wasm without JS host.

We use new names for the methods, instead of overloads, because older compilers look for those methods by name only. If an older compiler gets a newer library on the classpath, and the methods with those names became overloaded, the compiler would crash.

In the commit, we do not change the compiler yet, to test that the deprecated methods are correct.

In the second commit, we change the compiler to use the new APIs.

---

This does not bring any immediate benefit. It's more for a long-term vision. But it also shouldn't hurt, besides the cost of maintaining a deprecated pair of methods. If we had had `NewLambda` all along, I think we would have designed this API using the Scala types to begin with. The `Reflect` object never pretended to be Scala-agnostic, since its public API is full of Scala types anyway.

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Laravel Framework XSS in Blade templating engine

A security researcher has disclosed a possible XSS vulnerability in the Blade templating engine.

Given the following two Blade templates:

resources/views/parent.blade.php:

@section('content')
<input value="{{ $value }}">
@show

resources/views/child.blade.php:

@extends('parent')

@section('content')
<input value="{{ $value }}">
@endsection

And a route like the following:

Route::get('/example', function() {
    $value = '//localhost/###parent-placeholder-040f06fd774092478d450774f5ba30c5da78acc8## onclick=location.assign(this.value);//';

    return view('child', ['value' => $value]);
});

The broken HTML element may be clicked and the user is taken to another location in their browser due to XSS. This is due to the user being able to guess the parent placeholder SHA-1 hash by trying common names of sections. If the parent template contains an exploitable HTML structure an XSS vulnerability can be exposed.

This vulnerability has been patched by determining the parent placeholder at runtime and using a random hash that is unique to each request.

As described in #206 it's theoretically possible to cause overflows when either Karma is issued via `mint()` or `setReward()` because both functions don't take the supply of the other "domain" into account.

This commit fixes this by performing an arithmetic operation on `super.totalSupply()`, `totalDistributorAllocation` and the newly issued `amount`.

If there's an overflow, the code will cause an overflow and reverts. This ensure overflows can't happen *after* rewards have been issued.

Closes #206

author: sgress454
body:
For #28727

## Details

[This patch](https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/commit/866d8bcc0073cf7837d60d43eec0b54ad718375f) was intended to ensure that Fleet Desktop was always run with the currently-logged-in user. This patch didn't take Nudge into account, and it is now causing a command like sudo -u /usr/bin/open /path/to/nudge to execute, which fails.

This PR fixes the issue by checking whether `opts.user` is populated, and if not, falling back to the previous behavior for opening apps.

## Testing

I tested that Desktop still opens with this, so it at least doesn't break that.  Discussions ongoing re: how to test Nudge.

author: 13bfrancis
body: ## Purpose This is to resolve an issue which was exposed in our recent production deploy and any new deploy without the connectors already running. Essentially they were only being given 1024 MB of ram and .25 CPU units which simply proved to not be enough and caused a critical crash of any newly created service when trying to process all information stored in seatool's database. ## How we got here? Landing on this spot was due to tireless investigation over the last few days with many team members and a lot of calls. We started by checking as much off of the list as we could. It started internally on the MAKO project. Reviewing the codebase, comparing val to production. That was the same so we moved on. Next we tried to see if there was an issue with seatool and establishing a connection to there system. Due to work from Angel and his team we were able to get on a call with the Leidos data center and eliminate all possibilities there. We, went through and established that bigmac could talk to and communicate with seatool, looked at the activity and expensive queries (thanks to the leidos team for getting the proper accounts to do this with). We also had people on the ground trying a variety of different solutions in the seatool connectors code which is the mechanism that sits between seatool and bigmac. And finally after a lot of research and many calls we found language which a screenshot shows below to indicate there was an issue with memory allocation in one of the connectors. Upon pulling that string we landed here on a solution that just increases defaults to something more realistic for the production environments. #### Related Issues this helps resolve https://jiraent.cms.gov/browse/OY2-34437 ## Approach Upon further investegation of the ECS tasks that were getting killed it became known that a out of memory crash was occuring. So the solution was to simply increase the amount of memory and CPU given to the ECS task for Debezium and for KSQL.

Refactored the src/ directory to improve project organization, maintainability, and scalability. This includes restructuring folders for clear separation of concerns, removing unnecessary or duplicate files, and resolving case-sensitivity issues that could cause cross-platform errors.

- Ensured that each folder has a clear, single responsibility (e.g., assets/ for static files, features/ for feature-specific logic, etc.).
- Removed or renamed folders/files with conflicting casing to prevent import errors on case-insensitive filesystems.
- Maintained entry and test setup files at the root of src/ for clarity.

author: jeafreezy
body:
### What does this PR do?

This PR revamps the Start Mapping UI with improved prediction handling, dropdown performance (via Shoelace), and support for XYZ, TMS, and TileJSON. It also adds model feedback indicators, enhances form feedback, and refines the training dataset flow.

### Minor Features

1. **Model Feedbacks**

Model feedbacks are now visible for models with more than 0 feedbacks. A comment icon is rendered on each feature that has feedback.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa6576de-ac12-49a5-bd8a-53d1e0e7646c

2. **Improved Training Dataset Page**
- Support for multiple tile services (XYZ, TMS, TileJSON).
- Option to preview TileJSON if available.
- Automatic detection and zooming to bounds for OpenAerialMap (OAM) TMS sources.
- Separation of the create training dataset step from the continue to processing step.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f848de0-29af-483f-9be0-4e75cbee48e9


### Enhancements

1. **Copy Button Feedback**

- Tooltips now notify users when text is copied.
- Replaced alert() with animated, componentized feedback.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4683ebdb-2161-47c8-8560-343d2233fe08

2. **Dropdown performance** 

- Dropdown visibility is now handled natively by Shoelace.
- We removed unnecessary state toggling logic to prevent flickering/re-renders.
- The chevron icon no longer rotates, which was a costly visual effect. Based on UX reviews, it’s not commonly used, so this is acceptable.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9fc4dad-b9cc-451a-a97a-044933ed2084

3. **Enhanced Conflation Logic**
- Improved feature merging logic when new predictions overlap existing features.
- Ensures robustness when features are accepted, rejected, or untouched.
4. **Single Source of Truth for Prediction Features**
- Previously used 3 separate arrays (accepted, rejected, all).
- Now consolidated into a single array with a status property (untouched, accepted, rejected).
5. **Component Memoization**
- Optimized several components (e.g., dropdown triggers, selector panels) using useMemo to reduce unnecessary renders.
6. **Expanded Tile Service Support**
- Added support for:
   - XYZ (already supported)
   - TMS
   - TileJSON

7. Increased polling interval of the user profile from 10s to 15s to reduce network overhead while still supporting real-time notifications (since WebSockets are not yet in place).

8.  **Improved Input Fields:** Inputs now show visual feedback (color/border/icon) for valid and invalid states.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d16066bc-c92c-422b-9ce3-6a9b660edd81

10. Prediction features now support zoom level 18 (previously restricted to zoom 19 upward).

### How to Test

You can visit the Vercel deployment to test all these changes: https://f-a-ir-emmanuels-projects-1886bda9.vercel.app/

author: collindutter
body:
This PR overhauls a few components:
1. The argument parsing has been rewritten/restructured to have a cleaner top level namespace.

   Engine and asset update commands have been moved into `gtn self update` and `gtn assets update` respectively.

   ``` ❯ gtn --help usage: griptape-nodes [-h] [--no-update] COMMAND ...

    Griptape Nodes Engine.

    positional arguments:
      COMMAND
        init       Initialize a workspace.
        engine     Run the Griptape Nodes engine.
        config     Manage configuration.
        self       Manage this CLI installation.
        assets     Manage local assets (workflows, libraries, etc.).

    options:
      -h, --help   show this help message and exit
      --no-update  Skip the auto-update check.
   ```
2. The engine updater has been moved into a dedicated executable (`griptape-nodes-updater`). When performing an engine update, we exit the current process and call out to the updater. This resolves the issue on Windows where we can't update the currently running executable.

Closes #749
Closes #457

body:
## Summary
Speed up board evaluation and simplify code by using bitmap for trie traversal. Instead of checking whether the trie has a child for each of the neighbors, we use a bitmap of the children and iterate through that. Since we already have the `used` bitmap, a quick `AND` operation can restrict the neighbors we want to visit. We lose information about the order of neighbors.

- add child bitmap to Trie
- remove REC macros
- restrict the child bitmap by `used_` and iterate through it, popping a bit each time

title: "[pr] fix noise cancellation being disabled on headphones"
labels: 'bug'
assignees: '@Anmol202005'

---

## description

This PR fixes an issue where screenpipe would sometimes disable noise cancellation on headphones. The root cause was that we were using default audio configurations instead of the device's native highest quality configuration, which could override device-specific features like noise cancellation.

Changes:
- Modified `get_cpal_device_and_config` to use device's highest quality supported configuration
- Added proper handling of `SupportedStreamConfigRange` to preserve device features
- Improved configuration selection logic to prioritize sample rate and channel count

related issue: #59 

## how to test

1. Connect a pair of headphones with noise cancellation (like AirPods Pro, Sony WH-1000XM4, etc.)
2. Start screenpipe and verify that noise cancellation remains active:
   - On macOS: Check the Control Center to see if noise cancellation is still enabled
   - On Windows: Check the device properties in Sound settings
   - On Linux: Check the device settings in your audio control panel
3. Record some audio and verify that:
   - The noise cancellation remains active during recording
   - The audio quality is maintained
   - The device's native features are preserved

/claim #59
